drawings.description: figures : (C$_1$), au crayon et à l'encre, l'icosaèdre vu le long d'un axe passant par les milieux de deux arêtes opposées, sommets $u, v$, $u', v'$, $s, t$, $\Pi_{s,u}$, $\Pi_{t,v}$, … ; « ou » (C$_2$), la même vue en projection, sommets extérieurs $s'$, $u'$, $v'$, $t'$, points $\Pi_{t,u} = \Pi_{s',v'}$ (?), $\Pi_{t,v} = \Pi_{s',u'}$, $\Pi_{s,u} = \Pi_{t',v'}$, $\Pi_{s,v} = \Pi_{t',u'}$ ; (C$_3$), un schéma analogue plus petit, flèches vers $t'$ et $s'$
drawings.kind: icosahedron seen along an axis (three views)
drawings.notes: Redrawn from a fresh crop of p. 8 (issue 128), 1 unit = 1.8 mm. (C1) the icosahedron seen along the axis through the midpoints of two opposite edges, all 30 edges as on the page: the front edge t-s vertical, u and v at the sides, the four Pi vertices at the corners, the 17 visible edges solid; the hidden ones dashed: the two back side vertices (inside u and v) joined to the Pi corners and to the two ends of the back edge, which he draws a little above t and s (the back edge itself, on the line t-s, is not drawn separately). (C2) the same in projection: the back vertices s' (top), t' (bottom), v' (left), u' (right) outside, the four outer edges between them being the arcs of the circle (drawn as one closed curve; on the page it is in four heavy arcs with small gaps); the Pi points on the lines from the outer vertices, u and v on the sides of the Pi square, t and s computed as the crossings of the lines Pi-t-v and Pi-t-u (resp. Pi-s-v, Pi-s-u), which he draws straight; the vertical arrows to t' (up) and s' (down); the Pi labels with their equalities as on the page. (C3) the same scheme, smaller, with straight outer edges and arrows to t' and s'. Labels (C1), (C2), (C3) and "ou" placed as on the page. Pencil doublings drawn once. Left out: a small c-shaped mark at the centre of C2 and two small marks inside C2 just below s' and above t' (read as letters, not legible). The side labels of the back vertices are written like u' on both sides in C1 and on the left in C2; the redraw writes v' on the left, as the transcription and the equalities Pi_{t,u} = Pi_{s',v'} require (settled below). Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (maths): the back vertex on the left is v': the antipode of v lies on the side of u in this view, the equalities Pi_{t,u} = Pi_{s',v'} need it, and in (C_2) the left outer vertex is written v' on the page; the overinked letter at the left of (C_1) is read accordingly, and the redraw is unchanged. Not checked by a reader. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (page): the two small marks inside (C_2) under s' and above t' repeat the labels s' and t' of those vertices (the lower one reads t'), and the small hook at the centre is attached to no vertex; they stay left out, with no change to the figure. Not checked by a reader. Overlay check 2026-11-13 (issue 147, Claude claude-opus-5-5): the redraw, rasterised by the skill's previewer (not compiled: no TeX in the session), laid over the 300 dpi colour crop of the scan (250 ppi). The three views (C1 in pencil, C2 with its circle and axis, C3), their vertices, edges and labels lie on their ink to within about 1 unit. Matches the facsimile.

drawings.description: en marge gauche, un croquis : l'arête $a = \{s, t\}$, les sommets $u$, $v$, et les quatre sommets $\Pi_{s,u}$, $\Pi_{s,v}$, $\Pi_{t,u}$, $\Pi_{t,v}$ aux coins d'un rectangle. Les indices des $\Pi$ sont serrés et parfois surchargés ; ils sont donnés tels que l'argument les appelle (cf.\ page~8, où apparaît la même notation $\Pi_{s,u}$)
drawings.kind: neighbourhood of an edge of the icosahedron (planar)
drawings.notes: The edge a = {s, t} (vertical, in the middle), the vertices u, v on either side, and the four vertices Pi_{s,u}, Pi_{s,v}, Pi_{t,u}, Pi_{t,v} at the corners of a rectangle; s and t are joined to u, v and to their two Pi corners. Labels after the transcription (the indices of the Pi are cramped).

drawings.description: au crayon, très pâle, sous l'écriture du bas de la page : un croquis d'icosaèdre, dont on ne distingue que le contour (un sommet en haut, deux côtés qui en descendent, deux côtés verticaux) et quelques arêtes intérieures ; à droite, plus petit, un second croquis à peine visible.
drawings.kind: very faint pencil sketch of an icosahedron under the text
drawings.notes: The pencil is very faint and lies under the blue ink of the text. On the colour scan with the blue ink taken out and the grey stretched, the upper outline is clear -- the top vertex, the two sides falling from it to the upper left and upper right vertices, and the two vertical sides below them, down to the level of the last line of text; these five points and four strokes are drawn, in the pencil style, and they lie on the page within 1.5 mm. Left out because their ends cannot be fixed: a lower stroke joining the feet of the two vertical sides at about 45 mm, a fainter inner triangle pointing down (a nearly level stroke at about 26 mm from about 13 to 39 mm across, and two strokes from its ends down to about (30, -45)), and strokes from the top vertex and from the upper left vertex towards it; in the colour separation they can be seen but not followed to their vertices, so no reading of the inner edges is offered; the small second sketch at the right (two vertical strokes and a V between them) is left out likewise. Decided by a machine pass, 2026-11-12: the sketch is recorded as an icosahedron after the transcription's note and the subject of the page (the outline is the hexagon of the views of pp. 6 and 7). Not checked by a reader. Overlaid on the 400 dpi colour crop on 2026-11-12 (Opus 5.5): the drawn outline confirmed; the notes now say what the colour separation shows beyond it. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again. Overlay check 2026-11-13 (issue 147, Claude claude-opus-5-5): the redraw, rasterised by the skill's previewer (not compiled: no TeX in the session), laid over the 300 dpi colour crop of the scan (250 ppi). The drawn upper outline lies on its faint pencil within 1 to 1.5 units; nothing more of the sketch can be fixed on the scan. Still differs, as said above: the lower part of the sketch and its inner strokes are left out because their ends cannot be fixed under the ink of the text.

drawings.description: en haut, (A$_1$) : l'icosaèdre vu le long de l'axe $o o'$ — un décagone dont les sommets sont alternativement $s_4, s_3, s_2, s_1, s_0$ et $s'_1, s'_0, s'_4, s'_3, s'_2$, le pentagone des $s_i$ et les cinq rayons de $o$ vers les $s_i$ en trait plein, le pentagone des $s'_i$ et les rayons de $o'$ vers les $s'_i$ en tirets, $o$ et $o'$ confondus au centre ; à droite, après « ou », la même chose en projection : le pentagone extérieur $s'_0, \ldots, s'_4$, le pentagone intérieur $s_0, \ldots, s_4$ autour de $o$, chaque $s'_i$ joint à deux $s_j$.
drawings.kind: icosahedron along a 5-fold axis: decagon view and pentagon-in-pentagon projection
drawings.notes: Left: the ten vertices of the decagon computed once; solid: the decagon, the pentagon s_4 s_3 s_2 s_1 s_0 and the five radii from the centre o (the heavy point) to the s_i; dashed: the pentagon s'_1 s'_0 s'_4 s'_3 s'_2 and the five radii to the s'_i, which meet not at o but at the small cross just above and right of it (the point o', labelled beside it), as on the page; the label o below the heavy point. That is all 30 edges of the icosahedron (10 + 5 + 5 + 5 + 5). Right, after « ou »: outer pentagon s'_i, inner pentagon s_i, the centre o joined to the five s_i, each s'_i joined to its two neighbours among the s_j (25 edges; the five edges to o' are not in this figure; the arrow and o' under it are the text's). Labels as on the page, with the circled (A_1) at the left. The heavier strokes of the page (the side s_4 s_3, some radii) are not distinguished. Overlaid on the 400 dpi colour crop on 2026-11-12: the earlier redraw sent the dashed radii to o; on the page they go to the cross o', 2 mm up and right of o: corrected, and the cross drawn; s_1 of the right figure moved 1 mm. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: au milieu, (A$_2$) : deux pentagones emboîtés, $s'_0, \ldots, s'_4$ à l'extérieur et $s_0, \ldots, s_4$ à l'intérieur autour de $o$, chaque $s'_i$ joint à deux $s_j$ ; de chaque $s'_i$ part vers l'extérieur une flèche marquée $o'$ (le sommet $o'$ rejeté à l'infini).
drawings.kind: icosahedron projected from the vertex o-prime: two nested pentagons, arrows to o-prime
drawings.notes: As on the page: the outer pentagon s'_0 ... s'_4, the inner pentagon s_0 ... s_4, the centre o joined to the five s_i, each s'_i joined to its two neighbours among the s_j (the 30 edges of the icosahedron, the five through o' drawn as arrows): on the page these edges run as five long straight lines (s'_1 s_3 s_2 s'_4, s'_0 s_3 s_4 s'_2, s'_0 s_2 s_1 s'_3, s'_1 s_4 s_0 s'_3, s'_4 s_1 s_0 s'_2), which the computed vertices reproduce; the five edges from o are short curved strokes on the page, drawn straight. Five arrows pointing outwards, one from each s'_i, each labelled o'. Labels as on the page, with the circled (A_2) at the lower left; the label s_3 is written over a struck letter. Heavier strokes of the page (the sides at s'_0, some inner edges) are not distinguished. Overlaid on the 400 dpi colour crop on 2026-11-12: the centre o moved 1.4 mm up and right, onto the junction of his strokes; the rest within 1 mm. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: en bas, sous le trait horizontal, deux icosaèdres en perspective, vus à peu près le long d'un axe passant par les centres de deux faces opposées : à gauche un petit, sans lettres ni arêtes cachées ; à droite un grand, arêtes cachées en tirets, les six sommets du contour notés $a$ (en haut), $b'$, $c$, $a'$ (en bas), $b$, $c'$, les sommets intérieurs portant de petites lettres ($w$, $u$, $a$ pour la face avant ; $u$, $u'$, $w'$ pour la face arrière) de lecture douteuse.
drawings.kind: two icosahedra in perspective, one with hidden edges and named vertices
drawings.notes: Both figures are drawn from their vertices as read and the edge list of the icosahedron in this view: the hexagonal outline, the front face, and three edges from each vertex of the front face to the outline (18 visible edges); for the large one also the back face and its nine edges to the outline, dashed (30 edges in all). Every edge of the page is there and nothing is added: on the page the small figure shows the 18 visible edges only. Still differs: the six small inner letters of the large figure, which are tiny and partly covered by ink -- they are placed as read (front face: w at the left, u at the right, a at the bottom; back face: u at the top, u' at the left, w' at the right), and the transcription itself marks these identifications as doubtful; the outer label at the upper left, read c' here (the transcription's list has a'' and no c'). Decided by a machine pass, 2026-11-12: outline letters a, b', c, a', b, c' (opposite vertices carry the same letter with and without a prime, which fits a top, a' bottom, b lower left against b' upper right, and so c' upper left against c lower right). Not checked by a reader. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again. Overlay check 2026-11-13 (issue 147, Claude claude-opus-5-5): the redraw, rasterised by the skill's previewer (not compiled: no TeX in the session), laid over the 300 dpi colour crop of the scan (250 ppi). Both icosahedra, their dashed hidden edges and the outer letters lie on their ink to within about 1 unit; the edges he inked heavily (the outline a - c', a - b' and a' - b, c' - w, b' - u, and the front triangle's sides w - a and u - a) are now drawn heavy. What still differs is only the reading of the six tiny inner letters, as said above.

drawings.description: en haut, (B$_1$) : l'icosaèdre en perspective, vu le long d'un axe passant par les centres de deux faces opposées, arêtes cachées en tirets ; sommets du contour $u_1$ (en haut), $v'_1$, $w_1$, $u'_1$ (en bas), $v_1$, $w'_1$ ; face avant $w$, $v$, $u$ ; face arrière $u'$, $v'$, $w'$.
drawings.kind: icosahedron in perspective along a 3-fold axis, named vertices
drawings.notes: Drawn from the twelve vertices as read and the edges of the page: the hexagonal outline u_1, v'_1, w_1, u'_1, v_1, w'_1; the front face w, v, u and its nine edges to the outline, solid; the back face u', v', w' and its nine edges to the outline, dashed (30 edges). Labels as on the page (outer ones outside the outline, inner ones beside their vertices). Stroke weights are not reproduced. The transcription's note lists some of the names with a question mark (« w'_1 (?) »): the upper left vertex is read w'_1 here, the upper right v'_1, which fits the rule of the page (T, T_1, T'_1, T' with opposite vertices x and x'). Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: en bas, (B$_2$) : une construction en perspective de l'icosaèdre — la moitié avant du solide, sommets $a$, $c'$, $b'$, $w$, $v$, $b$, $u$, $c$, $a'$, prise dans un réseau de longues droites qui concourent en trois points de fuite (deux en haut, à gauche et à droite, un en bas) ; à gauche, un triangle hachuré, pointe en bas.
drawings.kind: perspective construction of the icosahedron with vanishing lines; hatched triangle
drawings.notes: Drawn: the nine named vertices and the edges between them that the page shows (c'-a, a-b', c'-w, a-w, a-v, w-v, v-b', c'-b, w-b, w-u, v-u, v-c, b'-c, b-u, u-c, b-a', c-a', and u-a' dashed), with their letters; the three vanishing points and the three long lines joining them (in ink on the page, like the rest); the hatched triangle at the left with the horizontal stroke across it. Left out: the other construction lines, some twenty long strokes from the vanishing points through the vertices and beyond, which cross one another over the whole figure and could not be assigned one by one; the circled label (B_2) is given at the lower left. Still differs: which vertices each construction line passes through is not established, so the perspective construction itself is not reproduced, only its frame; the hatching of the small triangle was a pattern over the whole triangle (redrawn on 2026-11-14, below). Decided by a machine pass, 2026-11-12: the two inner vertices of the upper row are read w (left) and v (right) and the middle one of the lower row u, as on (B_1). Not checked by a reader. Overlaid on the 400 dpi colour crop on 2026-11-12: every vertex, label and the frame lie within 1 mm of the page; the three long lines of the frame were in the pencil style, but they are in the same blue ink as the figure, and are now drawn plain. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again. Overlay check 2026-11-13 (issue 147, Claude claude-opus-5-5): the redraw, rasterised by the skill's previewer (not compiled: no TeX in the session), laid over the 300 dpi colour crop of the scan (250 ppi). The frame of three long lines, the icosahedron, its letters and the hatched triangle lie on their ink to within about 1 unit. Still differs, as said above: the many construction lines of the perspective are not reproduced, only the frame, and the hatching covered the whole small triangle (redrawn on 2026-11-14). 2026-11-14, Claude Opus 5.5, issue 147 second pass: the hatching of the small triangle redrawn stroke by stroke from the 400 dpi colour scan on a gridded crop at 36 pixels per unit: it is a zigzag of eleven blue strokes, most of them above the horizontal stroke, two running below it towards the lower vertex; the horizontal stroke follows its slight bend. Overlay with the local TikZ interpreter (not compiled: no TeX in the session): the drawn strokes lie on their ink to within about one unit. Still differs: where the zigzag is densest, between the middle of the horizontal stroke and the right side, two or three of its strokes run together and are not all separated; the construction lines of the perspective are not reproduced, only the frame.

drawings.description: en bas à gauche, dans un cercle : l'icosaèdre projeté sur le plan d'une face — $u'$, $v'$, $w'$ sur le cercle, puis le triangle $w'_1$, $v'_1$, $u'_1$, pointe en bas, les points $u_1$, $v_1$, $w_1$ au milieu de ses côtés, et au centre le petit triangle $w$, $v$, $u$.
drawings.kind: icosahedron projected on the plane of a face (Schlegel diagram) inside a circle
drawings.notes: Drawn from its structure, with the points placed as on the page: u', v', w' on the circle, whose three arcs stand for the sides of the outer face; the triangle w'_1, v'_1, u'_1; u_1, v_1, w_1 at the middles of its sides (as on the page, where each of these sides is one stroke through the middle point); the inner triangle w, v, u on the middles of the triangle u_1 v_1 w_1. Edges: each outer vertex to two vertices of the second triangle and towards one of u_1, v_1, w_1; the sides of the second triangle (two edges each); the six edges from u_1, v_1, w_1 to w, v, u; the three edges w-w'_1, v-v'_1, u-u'_1; the inner triangle: with the three arcs, the 30 edges of the icosahedron. As on the page, five strokes stop short of the vertex they go to: the three from u', v', w' towards u_1, v_1, w_1 (5 to 8 mm short) and the two from v' and w' towards u'_1 (4 to 6 mm short, leaving a gap on either side of u'_1). On the page the straight lines u'-v' and u'-w' pass through w'_1 and v'_1 and the line v'-w' through u'_1, as here. Labels as on the page; the three innermost letters are tiny and are given after the note of the transcription (w, v at the top, u at the bottom). Stroke weights not reproduced. Overlaid on the 400 dpi colour crop on 2026-11-12: the earlier redraw ran those five strokes to their vertices; they now stop where he stopped them; the circle moved 0.7 mm up and made 0.4 mm smaller. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: en bas à droite, à l'encre épaisse sur un tracé au crayon : un icosaèdre vu de face sur une arête, ses douze sommets visibles, une arête cachée horizontale en tirets ; au-dessus, un petit croquis de trois cercles qui se recoupent autour d'un petit polyèdre.
drawings.kind: icosahedron seen edge-on (ink over pencil); three overlapping circles round a small polyhedron
drawings.notes: Large figure: the twelve vertices as read and the 27 inked edges that can be followed between them (outline: top, two upper corners, two lower corners, bottom; inside: the upper centre on the top horizontal, a horizontal edge between two middle vertices with a vertical edge under each, the lower centre and the edges to it), and the dashed horizontal between the two lower corners. Small sketch above: three circles overlapping two by two and, where they meet, a small hexagonal outline with a triangle inside it. Left out: the pencil underdrawing round the large figure (a looser outline and a frame, which the transcription reads as a cube), several short dashed strokes inside it, and the inner strokes of the small polyhedron. Still differs: the edge list of the large figure is what the ink shows, not a checked icosahedron (27 solid edges and one dashed are drawn; the page may hold two or three more under the heavy ink); on the page six of its inner edges (the hexagon round the middle: from the two middle vertices up to the upper centre and down to the lower vertical edges, and from these to the lower centre) are in black ink and the rest in blue felt pen, which the redraw does not distinguish; the small sketch is schematic. Decided by a machine pass, 2026-11-12: the heavy figure is recorded as an icosahedron seen along an axis through the middle of an edge, the pencil frame round it not being legible as a cube with its edges. Not checked by a reader. Overlaid on the 400 dpi colour crop on 2026-11-12: the large figure lies on the page within 1.5 mm; in the small sketch the upper left circle was 3 mm too low and the right one 1.5 mm too far left, and the top vertex of the small hexagon 4 mm off: corrected. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again. Overlay check 2026-11-13 (issue 147, Claude claude-opus-5-5): the redraw, rasterised by the skill's previewer (not compiled: no TeX in the session), laid over the 300 dpi colour crop of the scan (250 ppi). The large figure lies on its ink to within about 1 unit; the circles and the small polyhedron of the sketch to within 1 to 2 units. Still differs, as said above: the edge list of the large figure is what the ink shows (two inks not distinguished), and the small sketch is schematic.

drawings.description: en haut à gauche, (B$_3$) : la même projection que la figure circulaire de la page~7, au crayon — $u'$, $v'$, $w'$ aux sommets d'un grand triangle, puis $w'_1$, $v'_1$, $u'_1$, puis $u_1$, $v_1$, $w_1$, et au centre le petit triangle $w$, $v$, $u$ ; au-dessus, à l'encre épaisse, un petit icosaèdre dans un cercle.
drawings.kind: icosahedron projected on the plane of a face (Schlegel diagram); small icosahedron in a circle
drawings.notes: (B_3): the twelve vertices as read and the 30 edges of the projection, drawn in pencil as on the page (the figure is in pencil, its letters in blue felt pen): the outer triangle u' v' w'; each outer vertex joined to two of w'_1, v'_1, u'_1 and to one of u_1, v_1, w_1; the hexagon w'_1, u_1, v'_1, w_1, u'_1, v_1; the six edges from u_1, v_1, w_1 to the inner triangle w, v, u; the three edges w-w'_1, v-v'_1, u-u'_1; the inner triangle. Every one of these edges is on the page. Labels as on the page, with (B_3) at the left. Above, in blue felt pen: the circle and, inside it, the icosahedron drawn from six points read on the circle and a front triangle, with the 18 visible edges of that view. Still differs: the small figure is very heavily inked and its inner edges are a reading by structure, not stroke by stroke (on the page the front triangle and the lower sides are clear, the upper sides of the hexagon are not); two thin strokes that cross the circle at the upper right are left out. Decided by a machine pass, 2026-11-12: the small figure is drawn as the view of pp. 6 and 7 (hexagonal outline, front face); either reading gives an icosahedron in a circle. Not checked by a reader. Overlaid on the 400 dpi colour crop on 2026-11-12: every vertex of (B_3) within 1 mm of the page; its strokes, which are pencil, are now in the pencil style. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again. Overlay check 2026-11-13 (issue 147, Claude claude-opus-5-5): the redraw, rasterised by the skill's previewer (not compiled: no TeX in the session), laid over the 300 dpi colour crop of the scan (250 ppi). (B_3), the circle and the small icosahedron lie on their ink to within about 1 unit. Still differs, as said above: the inner edges of the heavily inked small figure are a reading by structure, and two thin strokes across its circle are left out.

drawings.description: en marge gauche, un petit croquis à l'encre épaisse : un pentagone, avec à son sommet inférieur gauche un coin rempli de noir (un repère) d'où un trait sort vers la gauche ; deux petites marques, $\sigma_0$ à l'intérieur et $\sigma_2$ sous le sommet.
drawings.kind: pentagon with a blackened flag at one vertex
drawings.notes: As on the page: the pentagon drawn in the strokes he left: the left side, the top side and the right side in one run; the lower right side as a separate stroke that stops short of the right corner; of the lower left side only its end near the bottom (its other end is under the flag); the blackened quadrilateral inside it at the lower left corner (a flag: vertex, edge, face), filled solid as on the page; the stroke leaving the corner towards the left; the marks sigma_0 (inside, right of the flag) and sigma_2 (under the corner). A third small mark inside the pentagon, above the flag, is drawn as it stands: a hooked stroke and a short upright, written like the sigma_0 beside the flag (a hooked stroke and its index), so presumably sigma_1, the flag being vertex, edge and face; it is not labelled, the transcription naming only sigma_0 and sigma_2. The two labels are tiny and are given after the transcription. Overlaid on the 400 dpi colour crop on 2026-11-12: the earlier redraw closed the pentagon and hatched the flag; the sides are now the strokes of the page and the flag is solid. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again. Overlay check 2026-11-13 (issue 147, Claude claude-opus-5-5): the redraw, rasterised by the skill's previewer (not compiled: no TeX in the session), laid over the 300 dpi colour crop of the scan (250 ppi). The strokes of the pentagon, the solid flag, the stroke leaving the corner and the two labels lie on their ink to within about 1 unit; the mark above the flag, earlier left out, is added. Disagreement: the transcription names two marks, sigma_0 and sigma_2; the page has a third, presumably sigma_1 (docs/review/transcription-readings-128-2026-11-12.md, issue 145). Matches the facsimile.

drawings.description: à gauche, un dessin de l'icosaèdre en perspective, arêtes cachées en pointillé ; sommets marqués $u_1$, $w_1'$, $u'$, $v_1'$, $w$, $v$, $v_1$, $w_1$, $u = s$, $u_1'$, $w'$, $v'$ ; un triangle fondamental hachuré, de sommet $s$, porte sur ses côtés les marques $\sigma_0$, $\sigma_1$, $\sigma_2$
drawings.notes: Icosahedron with its hidden edges dashed; vertices u_1, w_1', v_1', v_1, w_1, u_1' on the outline, w, v, u = s in front, u', v', w' behind. Encoded as polyhedron/1 with the labels of the page (u=s for the front vertex); the 12 dashed edges are read from scattered dashes and checked against the icosahedron (every vertex of degree 5). The hatched fundamental triangle with apex s carries sigma_0, sigma_1, sigma_2 on its sides.

checks.name: icosahedron (vertices as labelled on the page)

drawings.description: dans la marge gauche, trois croquis : un pentagone de sommets $t = \tau$, $u$, $v$, $\tilde{u}$, $\tilde{v}$, de centre $s$, marqué $(\pi)$ ; sous lui, une colonne de paires fléchées en cycle, $\{s, u\} \to \{s, v\} \to \{s, \tilde{u}\} \sim \{t, v\}$, $\{s, \tilde{v}\} \sim \{t, u\}$, au-dessus d'un premier essai biffé ; plus bas, un fragment d'icosaèdre de sommets $u$, $v$, $w$, $u_1$, $v_1$, $w_1$, l'arête $\{u, v\}$ épaissie, et le cycle $\{u, w_1\} \to \{w_1, v\} \to \{v, w\} \to \{w, u\}$
drawings.kind: pentagon, cycle of pairs, fragment of icosahedron (margin)
